title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions with Like Denominators
seo_title: Grade 4 Adding and Subtracting Fractions Worksheets (TEKS 4.3E, 4.3F, STAAR)
standard_text: 4.3E represent and solve addition and subtraction of fractions with equal denominators using objects and pictorial models that build to the number line and properties of operations; 4.3F evaluate the reasonableness of sums and differences of fractions using benchmark fractions 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, and 1, referring to the same whole
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 fraction worksheets for Texas TEKS 4.3E and 4.3F: add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators, check with benchmark fractions, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Same denominator: add or subtract the numerators, keep the denominator.
key_sub: Check with benchmarks 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and 1. Rename a whole to subtract mixed numbers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • With equal denominators, the pieces are the same size. Add or subtract the numerators and keep the denominator: 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8.
  • For mixed numbers, add or subtract the wholes and the fractions. Rename 1 whole as 8/8 when you need more eighths.
  • Check with benchmarks 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and 1: 3/8 + 4/8 is a bit less than 1.

Examples

Example

3 1/6 − 1 5/6

You cannot take 5/6 from 1/6.

Rename: 3 1/6 = 2 7/6.

2 7/6 − 1 5/6 = 1 2/6

Answer: 1 2/6

Example

Is 5/8 + 1/8 close to 3/4?

5/8 + 1/8 = 6/8

6/8 = 3/4

Answer: yes, exactly 3/4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the denominators: 1/4 + 2/4 = 3/8Keep the denominator. Only the numerators change.
Not renaming a whole: 3 1/6 − 1 5/6 = 2 4/6Rename 1 whole as 6/6 first.
Skipping the estimateCompare with 1/2 or 1 to see if the answer makes sense.

faq.a: Represent and solve addition and subtraction of fractions with equal denominators using objects and pictorial models that build to the number line and properties of operations.
Evaluate the reasonableness of sums and differences of fractions using benchmark fractions 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and 1, referring to the same whole.

faq.q: Why do the denominators stay the same?
faq.a: The denominator names the size of the pieces. Adding pieces of the same size does not change their size.

faq.q: How do you subtract mixed numbers?
faq.a: Subtract the fractions, then the wholes. If the first fraction is too small, rename one whole as a fraction first.

items.q: Gabriel hiked 2 34 miles in the morning and 1 24 miles in the afternoon. How many miles did he hike in all?
items.e: Add the fractions: 34 + 24 = 54. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 1 = 3. 54 is more than 1: 54 = 1 14. So 3 + 1 14 = 4 14 miles.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Harper ate 38 of the pizza, and her dad ate 28 of it. What fraction of the pizza is left?
items.e: First find how much was eaten: 38 + 28 = 58. The whole pizza is 88. Left: 88 − 58 = 38.

items.q: A recipe for granola bars uses 23 cup of oats and 23 cup of raisins. How many cups is that in all?
items.e: Same denominator, so add only the numerators: 2 + 2 = 4. Keep the denominator 3: 43. That is more than 1. Take out 33 = 1, so 43 = 1 13 cups.

items.q: Zoe drank 78 of a bottle of water. Camila drank 48 of a bottle the same size. How much more of a bottle did Zoe drink than Camila?
items.e: “How much more” means subtract: 78 − 48. Same denominator, so subtract only the numerators: 7 − 4 = 3. Keep the denominator 8: 38.

items.q: Isaac had a ribbon that was 4 14 feet long. He cut off 1 34 feet to wrap a gift. How many feet of ribbon are left?
items.e: 14 is less than 34, so rename 1 whole as 44: 4 14 = 3 54. Subtract the fractions: 54 − 34 = 24. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 1 = 2. The answer is 2 24 feet.

items.q: It rained 1 310 inches on Monday and 910 inch on Tuesday. How many inches of rain fell on the two days in all?
items.e: Add the fractions: 310 + 910 = 1210. The whole number is 1. 1210 is more than 1: 1210 = 1 210. So 1 + 1 210 = 2 210 inches.

items.q: Carlos practiced the piano for 1 34 hours on Saturday and 34 hour on Sunday. How many hours did he spend in all?
items.e: Add the fractions: 34 + 34 = 64. The whole number is 1. 64 is more than 1: 64 = 1 24. So 1 + 1 24 = 2 24 hours.

items.q: A board is 6 feet long. Mia cuts off a piece that is 2 34 feet long. How long is the part that is left?
items.e: There is no fraction to take 34 from, so rename 1 whole: 6 = 5 44. Subtract the fractions: 44 − 34 = 14. Subtract the whole numbers: 5 − 2 = 3. The answer is 3 14 feet.

items.q: Luis ran 3 34 miles. Mateo ran 2 14 miles. How much farther did Luis run than Mateo?
items.e: “How much farther” means subtract. Subtract the fractions: 34 − 14 = 24. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 2 = 1. The answer is 1 24 miles.

items.q: Liam needs 2 13 cups of milk to make pancakes. He has 1 23 cups. How much more milk does he need?
items.e: Subtract what he has from what he needs. 13 is less than 23, so rename 1 whole as 33: 2 13 = 1 43. Subtract the fractions: 43 − 23 = 23. Subtract the whole numbers: 1 − 1 = 0. The answer is 23 cup.
